newsitem.title: UK: LME copper buoyant, soars to six-month highs.
newsitem.headline: LME copper buoyant, soars to six-month highs.

text.p: Copper prices rallied to six-month highs in pre-market trading on Thursday, and dealers forecast more volatility due to closed U.S. markets.
Fresh buying and short-covering, some of it options-related, pushed London Metal Exchange (LME) copper to a high of $2,313 per tonne in early trading.
Three months copper was indicated at $2,305/10 at 1030 GMT, after Wednesday's positive London late close of $2,272.
"This is follow-through buying after the strong close, and there's some covering of the spreads which look set to get tighter today," a dealer said.
The LME cash/threes backwardation was trading at $280 in the morning, compared to around $250 on Wednesday.
Options continued to play a key role in the rally ahead of the declaration of the December date next week.
Dealers reported some buying of the upside of $2,500 December calls Tuesday morning.
"I think we'll certainly bring December $2,500 into play and they might even try to push that $50 higher in the next three to four working days. It's very rampant," a dealer said.
Volatility was expected to increase in a thin market, with New York's Comex market closed on Thursday and Friday due to the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday.
LME aluminium ticked up with copper to six-month highs in the morning, hitting a high of $1,558 per tonne, compared to Wednesday's close of $1,545.
Although aluminium was expected to continue absorbing strength from copper, the other metals were little affected so far.
Lead was up $2.00 at $696/8, but its upside was seen limited.

"Despite strong rallies in other base metals, lead -- which has already fulfilled all downside targets -- remains under consistent selling pressure still," said technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
Nickel eased $30 to $6,990/00 after losing ground previously this week following recent upticks in LME stocks.
Zinc was virtually unchanged at $1,076/78, while tin was off $20 at $6,075/95.
